raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8261.

With the pinned `transformers==5.12.1`, every processor call runs `ProcessorMixin._check_special_mm_tokens`, which does `list(ids).count(token_id)` on a tensor. That compares one scalar tensor at a time, so a long prompt pays ~0.5 s per call even when it has no image or video. huggingface/transformers#47580 (released in 5.15.0) fixes this by calling `tolist()` first.

Bumping transformers is blocked on the sglang / torch pins (see #8261, #8240), so this PR backports the fix inside `hf_processor`:

- `_check_special_mm_tokens_on_lists` converts `input_ids` to Python lists and then calls the upstream check, so the counting and the error message stay upstream's.
- `hf_processor` binds it to the processor instance only when transformers < 5.15.0 and the processor class does not override the check. With transformers >= 5.15.0 nothing changes.

Unlike the `return_tensors: null` workaround from the issue, this needs no config change and does not change what the processor returns.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+8261
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+_check_special_mm_tokens
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+%22transformers+5.15%22
  No open or closed PR references #8261 or this function. #8240 (transformers bump) was closed without merging and is a different approach.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

Environment: `uv sync --frozen --all-packages --extra cpu` (torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.12.1), `torch.set_num_threads(1)`.

Benchmark with `hf_processor("Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B")` + `build_multimodal_processor_inputs`, a text-only prompt of 131,073 tokens, median of 5 calls after warmup:

| | time per call |
| --- | --- |
| stock 5.12.1 | 0.800 s |
| this PR | 0.292 s |

Equivalence checks against the unpatched processor:
- text-only 131K prompt: `input_ids` and `attention_mask` identical
- image + text prompt: `input_ids`, `attention_mask`, `pixel_values`, `image_grid_thw`, `mm_token_type_ids` identical
- truncation that cuts image tokens (`truncation=True, max_length=10`) still raises the upstream `Mismatch in image token count` error

Unit tests (new `tests/utils/test_processor_mm_token_check_on_cpu.py`, picked up by the CPU workflow):

```
python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_processor_mm_token_check_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_tokenizer_normalize_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_audio_input_support_on_cpu.py
22 passed
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff format, mypy and the repo checks pass. The `autogen-trainer-cfg` hook could not run locally (hydra missing in the hook env); this PR does not touch any trainer config.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/utils/tokenizer/tokenizer.py`: add `_check_special_mm_tokens_on_lists`; bind it in `hf_processor` behind a `transformers < 5.15.0` gate, next to the existing `get_rope_index` binding.
- `tests/utils/test_processor_mm_token_check_on_cpu.py`: counts on tensor `input_ids`, mismatch still raises, upstream check receives Python lists.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks on the changed files (see Test).
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation. Not needed, no user-facing change.
- [x] Add unit test(s) to the CI workflow.
- [ ] Request CI in the `ci-request` channel (will do after opening).

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from transformers import ProcessorMixin
+
+from verl.utils.tokenizer.tokenizer import _check_special_mm_tokens_on_lists
+
+IMAGE_TOKEN_ID = 7
+
+
+def _processor():
+    return SimpleNamespace(image_token="<image>", image_token_id=IMAGE_TOKEN_ID)
+
+
+def test_counts_match_on_tensor_input_ids():
+    input_ids = torch.tensor([[1, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID, 2, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID], [1, 2, 3, 4]])
+    text = ["a <image> b <image>", "text only"]
+    _check_special_mm_tokens_on_lists(_processor(), text, {"input_ids": input_ids}, ["image"])
+
+
+def test_count_mismatch_still_raises():
+    # Truncation dropped one image token from the first sample.
+    input_ids = torch.tensor([[1, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID, 2]])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Mismatch in `image` token count"):
+        _check_special_mm_tokens_on_lists(_processor(), ["<image> <image>"], {"input_ids": input_ids}, ["image"])
+
+
+def test_upstream_check_receives_python_lists(monkeypatch):
+    seen = []
+
+    def record(self, text, text_inputs, modalities):
+        seen.append(text_inputs["input_ids"])
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ProcessorMixin, "_check_special_mm_tokens", record)
+    input_ids = torch.tensor([[1, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID]])
+    _check_special_mm_tokens_on_lists(_processor(), ["<image>"], {"input_ids": input_ids}, ["image"])
+    assert seen == [[[1, IMAGE_TOKEN_ID]]]

@@ -134,6 +134,22 @@ def build_multimodal_processor_inputs(
     return processor(**processor_inputs)
 
 
+def _check_special_mm_tokens_on_lists(self, text, text_inputs, modalities):
+    """Run ``ProcessorMixin._check_special_mm_tokens`` on ``input_ids`` converted to Python lists.
+
+    Before transformers 5.15.0 the check counts special tokens with ``list(ids).count(token_id)``
+    on tensors, which compares one scalar tensor at a time and costs ~0.5 s for a 128K-token prompt
+    even when it has no image or video. huggingface/transformers#47580 converts ``input_ids`` with
+    ``tolist()`` first; this backports that fix for the pinned transformers version.
+    """
+    from transformers import ProcessorMixin
+
+    input_ids = text_inputs["input_ids"]
+    if hasattr(input_ids, "tolist"):
+        text_inputs = {"input_ids": input_ids.tolist()}
+    return ProcessorMixin._check_special_mm_tokens(self, text, text_inputs, modalities)
+
+
